page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-80 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel Xeon processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 80 vCPUs mapped to 40 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The system is equipped with 320.0 GB of dedicated RAM, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per core. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache. It does not include any bundled local storage or GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core processing capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, scoring in the top 25% for both small-block cached reads at 4129.09 GB/sec and large-block uncached reads at 213.45 GB/sec. Single-core performance benchmarks, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core, fall within the average range. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512, and AES cryptography, which contribute to strong performance in software compilation and database operations.

While the instance excels at highly threaded workloads, it exhibits performance limitations for certain tasks. Large-scale LLM text generation using a 70B model is a notable bottleneck, performing in the bottom 10% with 2.55 tokens per second due to the lack of GPU acceleration. Qualitatively, the server offers high resource density and a balanced compute-to-memory ratio, making it a cost-effective choice for enterprise-grade general-purpose workloads. It is well-suited for multi-threaded software compilation, high-throughput Redis database operations, and medium-scale data processing, but is less optimal for workloads requiring local NVMe storage or heavy AI model inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-80 is a general-purpose server featuring 80 vCPUs and 320 GB of RAM, powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon processor with an x86_64 architecture. Built with 40 physical cores and hyperthreading, it delivers strong multi-core performance, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU benchmarks. Memory performance is equally robust, with high-bandwidth read and write capabilities. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, which limits its utility for large-scale AI inference, as evidenced by poor text generation speeds on 70B LLM models. However, it supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AES. This hardware profile provides a balanced, high-density resource configuration suitable for demanding multi-threaded workloads, including software compilation, database operations, and high-throughput Redis deployments.
